title: Spending tomorrow’s means today
odia: ଆଜି କୁରୁ କୁରୁ ହସୁ, କାଲି ଲଙ୍ଗଳ କାହିଁରେ ଚଷୁ ?
literal_meaning: Today you laugh merrily; tomorrow, what will you plough with?
explanation: The teasing question asks what will remain after today’s enjoyment. It warns against consuming the very means needed for tomorrow’s work. The pleasure is immediate, while the cost becomes visible only when work must resume.
meaning_odia: ଆଜିର ଆନନ୍ଦ ପାଇଁ କାଲିର ଜୀବିକାର ସାଧନ ନଷ୍ଟ କରିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Someone proposes selling essential work equipment to fund a lavish celebration; a relative answers with this question. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The digital witness supplies a story of burning a plough as feast fuel. Treat that as its illustration of the saying, not a verified event or origin. Its citation currently displays a script error.
